slides.prompt: Eight sentences fell out. How do we put them back?
slides.hint: Two stories: a light bulb and teleportation.
slides.notes: 60-min Tue lesson, sl_t3 (time assumed 60 min). Module pp.36-37 gapped text (P1P5, marks collected). Outcomes (teacher-kept): use the 4 checks on every gap; complete gaps 1-8 in books. 1M notes: noisy class, avoid role mechanics and competitions; fingers voting + brief partner talk only.

slides.prompt: Alina wanted to build a robot. Which sentence fits?
options: She joined a robotics workshop and practised every weekend.
Her school had a large science lab with new computers.
Many pupils enjoy watching robot videos online.
slides.answer: She joined a robotics workshop and practised every weekend.
slides.feedback: Same topic and same person doing the thing. B and C drift away.
slides.notes: CLUE 1 (topic) adapted from the 2E routine. Vote with fingers 1/2/3, then reveal. Module answers stay hidden for the marked activity.

slides.prompt: Mei adopted a stray kitten. Which sentence fits?
options: She fed it milk in a warm box.
Kittens are playful animals that like string.
Her brother cycled to the market that morning.
slides.answer: She fed it milk in a warm box.
slides.feedback: She and it carry Mei and the kitten forward.
slides.hint: Who is she? What is it?
slides.notes: CLUE 2 (who/what chain). Expected chain talk: Mei to she, kitten to it.

slides.prompt: The hall was dark. Then lamps lit up. What fits?
options: The electrician had fixed the old wires that morning.
Schools often hold ceremonies in big halls.
The lamps were made of glass and metal.
slides.answer: The electrician had fixed the old wires that morning.
slides.feedback: Only A explains dark before and light after.
slides.hint: Read before AND after the gap.
slides.notes: CLUE 3 (both sides). The important one: never read only the gap.

slides.prompt: Razak dreamed of travel with no traffic. Talk, then choose.
options: He had imagined a teleportation machine the night before.
Buses in his town were always crowded.
Many people travel to work by bus.
slides.answer: He had imagined a teleportation machine the night before.
slides.feedback: Prediction first: a dream explains the slow bus after.
slides.hint: Partner talk 30 seconds: dream or real?
slides.notes: CLUE 4 (predict before options). Enforce talk-before-vote; teleportation flavour links to Module p37.

slides.prompt: Hakim studied old bulbs. Which sentence fits?
options: He sketched an old bulb at the museum.
Edison was a famous inventor from America.
The museum displayed many kinds of lamps.
slides.answer: He sketched an old bulb at the museum.
slides.feedback: Edison in B shares a word but follows the wrong idea.
slides.hint: Same word does not mean best answer.
slides.notes: TRAP adapted from the 2E routine. Ask: which idea connects bulbs to the prize notebook?

slides.prompt: When you see a gap, what do you check?
items: Topic: what are we talking about?
Who or what: who are we following?
Before and after: what must connect both sides?
Predict the missing idea, then choose.
slides.notes: Rebuild the 4-check routine. Leave visible during bookwork.

slides.prompt: How are the module pages organized?
slides.answer: Gaps 1 to 4 use sentences A to D. Gaps 5 to 8 use sentences E to H.
slides.notes: Light Bulb p36 (LS 3.1.1/3.1.2) + Teleportation p37 (LS 3.1.1/3.1.2). No module answers revealed; books carry the activity.

slides.task: Do gaps 1 to 8 in your book. Use the 4 checks on every gap. Submit for marks.
slides.frame: 1 Topic? 2 Who or what? 3 Before + after? 4 Predict, then choose.
slides.notes: Individual marked activity (~20 min). P1P5, 8 marks. Collect books after.
Exit evidence, 2 min choral/oral. Gaps in recall reopen Thursday if needed.
